source.reportedIn: Kaufmann et al. (2020), Compatible Stress Field Design of Structural Concrete, Section 6.5, Tables 6.14, 6.15, 6.17
source.note: Pier caps tested inverted: specimen stands on four vertical supports (load cells), a single vertical force applied at the top with zero eccentricity (specimens S1-S5). P_u in the test report is the MEAN of the four reaction forces, i.e. one quarter of the total applied load. 8 specimens were tested; only S1-S5 (constant geometry, no load eccentricity) were analysed with the CSFM.

csfmSettings.materialFormat: mean measured properties, no safety factors (gamma = 1)
csfmSettings.comment: The repo solver's nonlinearCsfm.ts already runs at gamma = 1 (effectiveFcd(.,.,1.0), steel.fy direct), so the failureLoadFactor is a nominal prediction. Validation only requires feeding the mean material properties below.
csfmSettings.bookModelM0: default CSFM: mesh 10, eps_cu2 = 3.5 permille, tension stiffening on (Tension Chord Model). M0 is the comparator used here.

geometry.status: From Kaufmann et al. (2020): Fig. 6.22a (specimen geometry) and Fig. 6.23 (CSFM model of S1). Shared by S1-S5 (constant geometry). The total height 980 mm is cross-confirmed by Fig. 6.23, which gives the model height as 0.98 m.
shapeNotes: The pier cap is a stepped shape: a 1200 mm wide cap at one end (160 mm constant band), a 320 mm tapered transition, and a 640 mm wide stem (500 mm constant band). Total height 980 mm, out-of-plane thickness 500 mm (Kaufmann et al. 2020, Fig. 6.22a: b = 500).
Structural action (D-region): a concentrated load over the loading plate l_b at the stem end spreads through the depth to four supports under the wide cap end — i.e. pile-cap action.

The repo's buildPileCap produces a rectangular cap with 2x2 piles. It captures the load-spread action but not the taper; the cap is modelled at the 1200 mm wide envelope. The CSFM book model is 2D plane stress; the repo solver is a 3D space truss.

reinforcement.distributedVertical_Av: present but NOT modelled (works mainly in compression — book Section 6.5.3)

measured.failureMode: CC+FY (concrete crushing, preceded by slight yielding of main reinforcement)

specimens.outlierFlag: The book flags S5 as a likely abnormal experimental result: despite 50% more transverse reinforcement and a 20% larger loading plate than S4, its measured strength is lower. All CSFM models predict S5 unsafe. Treat S5 as a documented outlier.

bookM0Summary.conclusion: CSFM (default M0) predicts ultimate load of these D-region pier caps with a mean experiment/prediction ratio of 0.96 and CoV 0.13. Strut-crushing failures are predicted less precisely than reinforcement-yielding failures (expected; design codes compensate with a higher concrete safety factor).
